notes.note: Health row and panel finding of the router advertisement check: a link has a DHCPv6 scope but its routers set neither the M nor the O flag; {routers} are the link-local router addresses, {interface} the interface, {node} the node, {scopes} the networks of the scopes.

segment.source: The routers {routers} on {interface} of node {node} set neither the M nor the O flag, so the hosts on that link do not ask DHCPv6 and the scopes {scopes} serve nobody. Turn on M (addresses) or O (options only) in the router advertisements.

notes.note: Health row and panel finding of the router advertisement check: routers set O without M while a scope of the link has address pools; {routers}, {interface}, {node} and {scopes} as in the flags-off finding.

segment.source: The routers {routers} on {interface} of node {node} set the O flag without M, so the hosts on that link ask DHCPv6 for options only. That is right for stateless DHCPv6; turn on M if the hosts should get addresses from {scopes}.

notes.note: Health row and panel finding of the router advertisement check: routers set M on a link that no enabled DHCPv6 scope covers; {routers}, {interface}, {node} as before, {prefixes} the prefixes the routers advertise.

segment.source: The routers {routers} on {interface} of node {node} set the M flag for {prefixes}, but no enabled DHCPv6 scope covers that link, so the hosts ask a server that does not answer. Add a scope for the link or turn M off.

notes.note: Health row and panel finding of the router advertisement check: the check cannot listen for router advertisements; {node} is the node, {reason} why the raw socket cannot be opened.

segment.source: The router advertisement check cannot run on node {node}: {reason}. It needs the CAP_NET_RAW capability of the probe role on Linux.

notes.note: Tag on the one-line router advertisement panel of the leases page: how many findings the check has.
Heading of the router advertisement panel on the leases page.
State of the router advertisement check when the node has no probe role, so nothing listens for advertisements.

segment.source: Not checked: no probe role runs on this node

notes.note: State of the router advertisement check when it cannot run; {reason} is the cause.
State of the router advertisement check while the node listens for advertisements.
Accessible name of the table of the links heard by the router advertisement check.
Column header of the router advertisement table: the network interface of the link.
Column header of the router advertisement table: the routers heard, by link-local address.
Column header of the router advertisement table: the M flag (managed address configuration); keep the single letter.
Tooltip of the M column header.

segment.source: Managed address configuration: hosts ask DHCPv6 for addresses

notes.note: Column header of the router advertisement table: the O flag (other configuration); keep the single letter.
Tooltip of the O column header.

segment.source: Other configuration: hosts ask DHCPv6 for options such as DNS servers

notes.note: Column header of the router advertisement table: the prefixes the routers advertise.
Column header of the router advertisement table: the networks of the enabled DHCPv6 scopes of the link.
Column header of the router advertisement table: when the last advertisement was heard.
Shown in the router advertisement panel when the check watches but heard no advertisement.

segment.source: No router advertisement heard in the last hour

notes.note: Note under the router advertisement panel: DHCPv6 has no option for a default route.

segment.source: DHCPv6 never sets a default route: hosts take it from the router advertisements.

notes.note: Fact in the status strip of the leases page: the DUID of the DHCPv6 server; {duid} is the hexadecimal value in pairs with colons.
Tooltip of the server DUID fact in the status strip; {duid} is the whole value.

segment.source: The DUID this DHCPv6 server names itself with: {duid}
